inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average for the six months to 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim report note 12(b): 9,029m basic ex award-scheme/treasury shares + 134m dilutive options/awards = 9,163m). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the count is in fact shrinking (9,408m FY2024 -> 9,244m FY2025 -> 9,163m H1 FY2026) because buybacks (RMB73.3bn FY2025, RMB22.3bn H1 FY2026) exceed SBC by 2-3x, so the flat count is funded and mildly conservative. Issued shares at 30 June 2026: 9,092.2m including 84.3m held for the share award scheme.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report consolidated cash flow note 43(a): share-based compensation expenses add-back RMB31,859m (includes a one-off RMB4.0bn equity-settled charge for restructuring a commercial arrangement at an overseas subsidiary, AR p.18 and note), plus RMB954m withholding individual income tax on share option exercises (financing activities). The non-IFRS reconciliation's narrower 'equity-settled share-based compensation' figure is RMB25,660m; the broader cash-flow add-back is used because it is what OCF excludes. Forward SBC% anchored to the ex-one-off run-rate (3.7% FY2025, 3.3% H1 FY2026).
inputs.interest_income_note: Tencent classifies 'Interest received' (RMB14,534m FY2025; income-statement interest income RMB16,909m) in INVESTING activities and 'Interest paid' (RMB13,180m) in FINANCING, so reported OCF/FCF is already unlevered and excludes interest on the treasury. Nothing to strip from the flows; set to 0. Net cash on the narrow basis is RMB22.0bn, well under 1x the FCF base in any case. Dividends received from investees (RMB6,500m) are likewise in investing, so the investment portfolio's income is already out of the flows and the portfolio goes into the equity bridge once (matching-asset rule).
inputs.fx_note: CNY -> HKD 1.1721 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-10T03:38Z). All flows and per-share values are computed in RMB and converted at this rate; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD to match current_price. Parity check: Tencent's own RMB counter 80700.HK closed RMB361.8 on 2026-10-09; 361.8 x 1.1721 = HKD424.1 vs HKD424.8 observed on 0700.HK the same session (0.2% tie). Second check: TCEHY ADR (1 ADR = 1 share) USD54.6 at the US close x USDHKD 7.8472 = HKD428.5 (+0.9%, four hours after the HK close). Rate, direction and quote basis confirmed. refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate; re-fetch it on every rebuild.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z regular close (HKEX Friday session; valuation written Sunday 2026-10-11)
inputs.net_debt_note: At 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim, condensed balance sheet): cash and cash equivalents 206,930 + term deposits 267,999 (non-current 52,724 + current 214,275) = 474,929 gross cash; borrowings 298,942 + notes payable 154,021 = 452,963 total debt (the company's own 'Total debt' in the capital-risk note). Net cash RMB21,966m. The company's headline net cash of RMB58,191m additionally counts ~RMB36bn of 'highly liquid investment products held for treasury purposes'; those sit inside FVPL and are carried in the equity bridge (haircut), not here, so they are counted once. Restricted cash 7,729 excluded. Lease liabilities (13,366 non-current + 5,499 current = 18,865) excluded from debt under lease treatment (B). Net cash fell from RMB107.1bn at Dec-2025 on H1 capex of RMB107bn plus ~RMB60bn of AI compute prepayments and RMB41.6bn of dividends.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10-year CGB ~1.8% risk-free (Oct-2026), mature-market ERP 5.0% plus China country risk premium 1.5%, equity beta 1.05 -> cost of equity ~8.6%; pre-tax cost of debt ~2.9% (2.0-5.6% USD notes, RMB bank facilities) after tax ~2.4%; debt ~12% of capital at market (RMB453bn debt vs ~RMB3.3tn market cap) -> ~7.9%. Rounded UP to 8.5% for the VIE/Cayman structural claim and the offshore-holder perspective. No further premium is stacked: regulatory, geopolitical (1260H), gaming-approval and AI-capex-return risk are charged ONCE, in the bear scenario's flows and its 25% weight, and every scenario discounts at the same 8.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal RMB6,783m + interest ~RMB0.75bn FY2025; H1 FY2026 run-rate RMB3,977m per half = 1.0% of revenue) deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (RMB18,865m) EXCLUDED from net debt. Adjusted EBITDA is post-IFRS-16 (lease cost excluded, ROU depreciation in D&A), so da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 66,028 - 6,219 = 59,809 = 8.0% of revenue. Tencent's own FCF definition also deducts lease payments and 'media content payments'; the latter are inside the CSV's capex (purchase of intangible assets, RMB25.4bn FY2025), so the capex path carries them.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests charged ONCE in the bridge: RMB86,660m book value at 30 June 2026 deducted from equity value. Flows are consolidated. NCI share of profit was RMB4,959m in FY2025 (2.2% of total), so book is ~17x their earnings - a fair deduction. Minority-buyout payments (RMB4.2bn FY2025) are not separately modelled.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1/2: diversified operating company - games, social, advertising, fintech, cloud - with the non-US adaptations for dual currency, IFRS-16 leases, NCI and a very large non-operating investment portfolio). First valuation of this ticker; no prior model to reconcile against. BASE YEAR FY2025 (Dec year-end), year 1 = FY2026 which is 9 months elapsed at the valuation date; H1 FY2026 actuals (revenue +10.1%, adjusted EBITDA margin 45.1%, capex RMB107bn) anchor the year-1 drivers. AI CAPEX IS MODELLED EXPLICITLY, NOT MID-CYCLED: FY2025 capex was already 15.0% of revenue (vs 8-9% pre-AI) and H1 FY2026 was 26.7% of H1 revenue BEFORE ~RMB60bn of compute prepayments that sat in working capital and turned Q2 company-defined FCF negative (-RMB13.8bn; +RMB37.6bn ex-prepayments). The base capex path runs 30% of revenue in FY2026 (absorbing the prepayments), 25%, 20%, 17%, 15%, 14%, 13% and settles at 12.5% from FY2033 - a permanently higher steady state than the pre-AI era because 3-5 year-life compute must be continually refreshed - with D&A ex-ROU rising from 8.5% to 12.5% on a lag so that terminal capex = terminal D&A. This is the single most consequential judgment in the model; the bear case has the spend persist longer with no margin payoff, the bull case has it moderate faster with a margin payoff. EBITDA basis: Tencent's non-IFRS 'Adjusted EBITDA' (operating profit less interest income and other gains/losses, plus D&A, plus equity-settled SBC): 38.7% FY2023, 42.0% FY2024, 44.8% FY2025, 45.1% H1 FY2026. The engine subtracts SBC and the lease charge from this margin. CASH TAX: FY2025 cash tax RMB44.7bn = ~18% of the post-SBC, post-lease EBIT this build produces (statutory 25% offset by 15% HNTE/preferential rates, plus 10% withholding on remitted earnings and Pillar Two); path 18% -> 20% as preferential rates expire and remittances rise. WORKING CAPITAL: deferred revenue (+RMB6.2bn FY2025 on +RMB91.5bn revenue, ~7%; +13% FY2024) captured at 8% of the revenue CHANGE. SBC charged once: expensed in flows, count flat; buybacks value-neutral. Share count: fully diluted 9,163m from the latest interim. Non-operating assets: investment portfolio of RMB903bn at 30 June 2026 added in the equity bridge with 15-30% haircuts (see equity_bridge); its income (dividends received, share of associates' profit, fair-value gains) is already outside Adjusted EBITDA and outside OCF, so there is no double count. M&A spend (business combinations RMB11.5bn, associates RMB24.6bn FY2025) is NOT in the flows - treated as discretionary portfolio turnover funded by the portfolio itself; this is a mild generosity flagged in key_risks. Horizon 10 years because the year-5 owner-FCF margin is still rising as capex moderates and D&A catches up.

equity_bridge.item: Investments in associates and joint ventures (carrying RMB329,906m: associates 323,674 + JVs 6,232), less 25% holdco/disposal-tax haircut
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 interim balance sheet, notes 17 and 18. Listed associates' fair value RMB233,824m at 30 June 2026 (RMB349,313m at Dec-2025, before reclassifications of certain investees to FVOCI/FVPL on board-seat resignations). Haircut covers the holding-company discount the market applies to Tencent's portfolio, 10-25% tax on realisation, and the unlisted portion's valuation uncertainty.

equity_bridge.item: Listed / level-1-2 financial assets at FVPL and FVOCI (fair value RMB304,137m), less 15% haircut
equity_bridge.note: FVPL 247,923 + FVOCI 325,239 = 573,162 total at 30 June 2026 (note on fair-value hierarchy: level 1+2 = 573,162 - 269,025 level 3). Includes ~RMB36bn of treasury-purpose liquid products that the company counts in its own net cash; carried here instead so they are counted once. Haircut for realisation tax and holdco discount; these are quoted stakes (e.g. Kuaishou, Sea, Spotify, Pinduoduo-type positions) that the market already discounts inside Tencent's price.

equity_bridge.item: Unlisted / level-3 financial assets at FVPL and FVOCI (fair value RMB269,025m), less 30% haircut
equity_bridge.note: Level 3 = 213,994 FVPL + 55,031 FVOCI at 30 June 2026. Heavier haircut for mark uncertainty (convertible preferred shares of unlisted investees, whose remeasurement swung the share-of-associates line by RMB-10bn in Q2 2026 alone), illiquidity and disposal tax.
H1 FY2026 interim balance sheet, 30 June 2026. Charged once here; flows are consolidated.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR (17.0%, FY2022->FY2025) exceeds revenue (10.7%) and EPS (7.7%) by >30%: FY2022 equity was a trough after RMB-scale fair-value losses on the investment portfolio and the FY2021-22 dividends-in-specie (JD.com, Meituan stakes distributed to shareholders), so the equity series is a poor growth proxy here. Revenue 5-yr CAGR (9.3%) is used as the anchor; the base path starts above it (11% FY2026, consistent with H1 FY2026 +10.1% and Q2 +11%) and decelerates to 3% by year 10.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs end FY2025 (Dec). Owner-FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - capex) - cash-flow SBC add-back - lease principal (interest income is not in OCF): FY2020 110,238; FY2021 86,376; FY2022 63,024; FY2023 145,121; FY2024 132,680; FY2025 151,535 (RMB m). Owner-FCF 5-yr CAGR 6.6% vs reported-FCF 8.3%: SBC grew from RMB13.7bn to RMB31.9bn over the period (2.9% -> 4.2% of revenue), so part of the reported FCF growth was paid for in stock. The 3-yr owner-FCF CAGR of 34% is off the FY2022 trough (regulatory crackdown year) and is not a forward indicator. EPS is diluted IFRS EPS in RMB, distorted by fair-value swings on the portfolio; non-IFRS diluted EPS grew FY2024 24.9 -> FY2025 ~28.6 (+15%) on the company's basis.

base.narrative: Revenue +11% FY2026 (H1 actual +10.1%, Q2 +11%) decelerating 1pp/yr to 3% by FY2035: Marketing Services keeps compounding mid-teens on AI targeting and Video Accounts, games high-single-digit with International >10% and Domestic normalising after the FY2025 Delta Force surge, FinTech & Business Services ~10% with cloud accelerating on AI demand. Adjusted EBITDA margin holds ~45% (H1 FY2026 45.1%) then drifts to 46% as mix shifts to internally developed games, Video Accounts and cloud; AI opex offsets most of the gross-margin gain. Capex absorbs the AI build at 30% of revenue in FY2026 (including the ~RMB60bn of compute prepayments) and moderates to a 12.5% steady state by FY2033; D&A ex-ROU rises on a lag to the same 12.5%, so the terminal year is self-funding. Cash tax drifts 18% -> 20%. SBC 3.5% -> 3.0% of revenue.

bull.narrative: The AI capex cycle pays: Hy3/Yuanbao/WorkBuddy/CodeBuddy and the Xiaowei agent inside Weixin convert usage into advertising, cloud and subscription revenue, Marketing Services keeps growing 20%+ on closed-loop Mini Shop ads with ad load still below peers, International Games compounds >15% off the USD10bn base and Tencent Cloud's profit inflection continues. Revenue growth holds 10-12% for four years before decelerating to 4%. Adjusted EBITDA margin expands to 48% on mix and AI operating leverage. Capex moderates faster (to 11.5% of revenue) once the fleet is built, leaving a mature owner-FCF margin in the high-20s. No new regulatory shock; the 1260H listing stays reputational only.

bear.narrative: AI spend without an AI payoff, inside a tightening perimeter: capex stays above 20% of revenue through FY2029 as Tencent matches Alibaba/ByteDance compute spend and GPU export controls raise the cost per unit of capability, while Yuanbao/WorkBuddy monetisation lags; AI depreciation and R&D staff costs compress adjusted EBITDA margin to 41%. Revenue growth fades to 2.5%: NPPA approval slowdowns or renewed minor-protection campaigns cap domestic games, Douyin keeps taking ad share and consumer weakness caps FinTech. The 1260H designation hardens into broader US restrictions on capital-markets access or chips, and preferential tax rates expire (cash tax 22%). Terminal multiple capped at 15x; same 8.5% WACC so risk is charged once, in the flows.

scenario_narratives.base: Steady compounding through the AI build: revenue +11% in FY2026 decelerating to 3% by FY2035, adjusted EBITDA margin ~45-46%, capex peaks at 30% of revenue in FY2026 and settles at 12.5% from FY2033 with D&A catching up on a lag. Owner FCF is depressed to ~5% of revenue in FY2026 and recovers to the low-20s% by the terminal year. Axes: AI-ad targeting and Video Accounts (Marketing Services), International vs Domestic games growth, cloud's AI-driven acceleration, and the pace at which the compute build moderates.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI monetisation arrives: Hy3-powered applications, closed-loop Weixin commerce ads, International Games >15% and a cloud profit inflection hold revenue growth at 10-12% for four years and lift adjusted EBITDA margin to 48%; capex moderates to 11.5% of revenue by FY2032. Owner-FCF margin reaches the high-20s.
scenario_narratives.bear: Prolonged AI arms race with weak returns, gaming/platform regulation and a hardening US 1260H posture: growth fades to 2.5%, adjusted EBITDA margin compresses to 41%, capex stays above 20% of revenue through FY2029 and settles at 14%, cash tax rises to 22%, terminal multiple capped at 15x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: Tencent carries a stacked regulator/geopolitics dependency (NPPA game approvals, SAMR platform rules, the Pentagon 1260H designation reaffirmed June 2026, VIE/Cayman structure) plus an unproven thesis that the RMB250bn-a-year AI build earns its cost of capital - Q2 2026 company-defined FCF was negative and net profit grew 0.7% while revenue grew 11%. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: AI applications monetising, ads holding 20%+ growth, International Games compounding >15%, and no regulatory or US-policy shock. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House basis: owner FCF with SBC fully expensed, the AI capex step-up modelled explicitly year by year rather than mid-cycled (capex 30% of revenue in FY2026 settling at 12.5%, D&A catching up on a lag), leases charged as an operating cost, NCI deducted once, and the RMB903bn investment portfolio added to the bridge at a 15-30% haircut because its income is already outside the flows. Flows in RMB discounted at an 8.5% CNY WACC with no stacked risk premium; China regulatory, geopolitical and AI-return risk is charged once through a 25% bear weight. Per-share values computed in RMB and converted to HKD at 1.1721, verified against the 80700.HK RMB counter. The stock sits at the bottom of its 52-week range (411-664) because the market is pricing the FY2026 FCF collapse as if it were permanent; the model's answer depends on whether capex normalises, which is the central thing to monitor.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex path: every 1pp of permanently higher steady-state capex (12.5% base) costs roughly RMB14bn of terminal FCF; if the AI fleet needs 15%+ of revenue indefinitely (bear) the value falls sharply. Watch quarterly capex and the compute prepayment line.

Investment portfolio: ~RMB694bn after haircuts (~HKD89/share, ~21% of the price) rests on fair values that moved RMB-10bn in one quarter; a deeper China-tech drawdown or a larger holdco discount erodes it directly.

Regulatory/geopolitical: NPPA licence slowdowns, minor-protection rules, SAMR platform actions, and escalation of the US 1260H listing into chip, data or capital-markets restrictions are modelled only through the bear weight.

M&A and associate investments (RMB36bn in FY2025) are excluded from the flows on the assumption they are funded by portfolio turnover; if they are a recurring cost of growth, owner FCF is overstated by ~4-5% of the base.
Cash tax: preferential 15% HNTE rates and withholding-tax provisioning are policy-dependent; each 1pp on the cash tax rate is ~RMB4bn of terminal FCF.
FX: a 5% RMB move against HKD shifts every HKD figure 5%; fx_rate is not refreshed by refresh_price.py.
